title: The freezer balloon
hook: A balloon goes from room temperature into the freezer. How much does it shrink?

knows: that gases fill their containers and shrink when cooled
Celsius temperatures and that a kelvin temperature is the Celsius one plus 273
doesNotKnow: that gas volume is proportional to the absolute (kelvin) temperature at fixed pressure
why the kelvin scale starts at −273 °C

misconception: Celsius temperatures can be used directly, so cooling from 27 °C to a sub-zero freezer roughly halves the balloon (or more).
objective: The learner can explain that at fixed pressure a gas's volume is proportional to its kelvin temperature, so 300 K to 255 K shrinks 1.00 L to 0.85 L, and that the volume-temperature line points to zero at about −273 °C, the zero of the kelvin scale.

claims.text: At fixed pressure and amount, a gas's volume is proportional to its kelvin temperature (Charles's law).
claims.source: Charles's (Gay-Lussac's) law, ideal-gas limit: Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, ch. 1 (the perfect gas). Air in a balloon near room conditions follows it closely; the balloon skin is assumed to keep the pressure about constant.

claims.text: 1.00 L at 300 K becomes about 0.85 L at 255 K: it shrinks by 15%.
Gas scientists add 273 to a Celsius temperature to get kelvin: 27 °C is 300 K and −18 °C is 255 K.
claims.source: T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15 (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed., 2019): 300.15 and 255.15 K, rounded. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): BIPM SI Brochure: T/K = t/°C + 273.15; node 300.15 and 255.15, rounded to 300 and 255.

claims.text: Extended backwards, the straight volume line reaches zero at about −273 °C, which is 0 K, where the kelvin scale starts.
claims.source: From c1, V = 0 when T = 0 K; 0 K = −273.15 °C by definition of the Celsius scale (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed., 2019).

claims.text: Celsius has its zero at the freezing point of water.
claims.source: Historically defined by the ice point; now defined as T(K) − 273.15, which puts 0 °C within about 0.0001 K of water's normal freezing point (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.; CRC Handbook).

claims.text: A real gas such as the air in the balloon turns liquid long before it gets as cold as −273 °C.
claims.source: Nitrogen boils at 77 K (−196 °C) and oxygen at 90 K (−183 °C) at 1 atm (CRC Handbook, 'Physical constants of inorganic compounds'); even helium liquefies at 4.2 K. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): Normal boiling points N2 77.4 K, O2 90.2 K, He 4.2 K (CRC Handbook); all well above 0 K, so air liquefies long before -273 °C.

recall.question: A 2.0 L bag of air at 300 K is warmed to 330 K at the same pressure. Its volume is about…
recall.why: Volume goes with the kelvin temperature: 2.0 L x 330/300 = 2.2 L.
